critical_code_review_comments: request_visibility.py:_self_advance_clause() allows rows where source != 'advance' OR self_raised != true — this means legacy on-behalf advance rows that pre-date the self_raised flag (if any slipped past backfill_advance_visibility()) will fall back to the old behavior and remain visible to everyone. The startup backfill in approval_policy.py mitigates this, but a one-liner guard (treat missing self_raised flag on source='advance' rows as self_raised=True after backfill date) would be safer defense-in-depth.

project_requests_router.py list_requests()/summary() both duplicate the own_rows_clauses + apply_project_scope + apply_request_visibility composition (lines 331-336 and 400-403). Extract into a shared helper to keep the two visibility surfaces guaranteed-in-sync — otherwise a future tweak to one can silently diverge.

my_inbox_router._project_requests() applies apply_request_visibility but passes a {status: pending_approval} query; apply_request_visibility is correct here, but it also does NOT short-circuit for non-manager-log users meaning every inbox call runs an extra Mongo stage. Negligible, but consider caching request_visibility_clauses(user) per-request if the inbox endpoint becomes hot.
